decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Understanding Mineral Rights Valuation Near You
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 46119e11fd375db8f54ffe3d9150b6c2a54ca75cf1c56e53102a0bb36b6cb1c3; all 8 declared sources passed live access review.

MRX claims remain bounded to its current methodology, FAQ, and How It Works page; Railroad Commission claims preserve the separate GIS, query, well-record, county-record, identifier, and operational-data boundaries; and the GLO claim preserves the distinction between original grants, later county records, and current ownership.

The article uses no fabricated owners, buyers, contracts, deeds, prices, acreage, ownership decimals, tax results, offers, testimonials, success rates, or owner-specific title, legal, tax, accounting, appraisal, investment, or transaction conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Published DCF Methodology (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX methodology describes a directional DCF range with dated inputs, assumptions, limitations, and sensitivity, and separates asset range from offer consideration and expected owner net.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the methodology only for the disclosed directional framework, input-status discipline, sensitivity review, and transaction separation; it does not value a specific interest, establish ownership, or recommend a transaction.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Frequently Asked Questions (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX FAQ describes the review as educational, directional, and not certified, and states that a possible later MRX buyer relationship is disclosed when applicable.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the FAQ only for the professional boundary and potential economic-interest disclosure; it does not promise value, price, an offer, payment, or closing.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, How It Works (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX How It Works page describes the first-party intake sequence, the directional review boundary, and a separate path for reviewing a written offer.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page only to distinguish assessment intake from a complete written-offer comparison; it does not promise eligibility, a value, an offer, payment, acceptance, or closing.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Public GIS Viewer (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas describes its Public GIS Viewer as a map surface for oil, gas, pipeline, well, survey, lease, API, and related Commission-regulated data.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the viewer only for dated geographic and operational context; it does not treat map proximity or a displayed feature as proof of ownership, tract inclusion, formation rights, payment entitlement, reserves, future development, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, About Oil and Gas Data Queries (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas explains that its oil-and-gas queries cover distinct slices of the regulatory system, identifies available search fields, and states update schedules for several query surfaces.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the guide only to preserve query identity, identifiers, retrieval date, reporting scope, and update context; it does not infer title, owner allocation, reserves, future activity, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Well Records (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas well-records page describes available record types and lists county, lease or well name, operator, field, API or permit number, and survey or abstract information as useful retrieval details.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those fields only to route and identify operational records; it does not treat a well file as proof of an owner’s title, acreage, decimal, payment, tract inclusion, reserves, development, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Royalties FAQ (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas Royalties FAQ routes lease or royalty-agreement questions toward the courthouse in the county where the land is located and describes using RRC identifiers to retrieve production information.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the FAQ only to keep county conveyance records and Commission operational records in separate evidence lanes; it does not claim that either source alone resolves ownership, legal effect, payment entitlement, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Texas General Land Office, Minerals FAQ (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas General Land Office minerals FAQ distinguishes original land-grant records from later county conveyance records and cautions that descent from an original grantee does not alone establish current mineral ownership.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the FAQ only to route property-and-interest research and preserve the title boundary; it does not infer ownership, acreage, legal effect, or value from a surname, grant record, or family history.
